subject: Valora Health — Azure Private Plan commercial terms and procurement questions
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@valorahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Perez <tom.perez@valorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Valora Health - Azure Private Plan: commercial and procurement questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Valora's platform team is excited about Redwood's latency and the dedicated capacity model for our clinical inference workloads. Our procurement/legal team reviewed the standard Azure Private Plan offer and we have a few asks before we can issue an internal approval:

1) Data residency and logging: we need an explicit clause confirming that PHI will be processed only within the specified Azure region and that audit logs will be retained for 7 years.
2) SLA & remedies: the plan shows a 99.5% uptime target. Our SREs need a remedies schedule for sustained outages (>=30 minutes).
3) Indemnity and liability caps: Valora's counsel requests a liability cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months rather than a fixed amount.
4) Procurement path: can you confirm whether the private plan supports purchase via Azure Marketplace PO flow (merchant-seller routing) or if we must execute a standalone SOW/PO with Redwood?

I've attached a markup (Valora_Redlines_20260405.pdf) with inline comments. Can we set expectations on a timeline for counterterms? The procurement committee meets next Wednesday (4/8).

Best,

Maya Singh
Director, Vendor Management
Valora Health
Attachment: Valora_Redlines_20260405.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@valorahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Perez <tom.perez@valorahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Valora Health - Azure Private Plan: commercial and procurement questions

Maya — thanks for the clear markup and the heads up on timing. We're aligned on trying to get this in front of your committee before Wednesday. Quick answers up front: 

- Data residency & logs: Redwood supports region-scoped processing for Private Plans and we can commit to retaining audit logs for 7 years; I'll loop in legal for precise language.
- SLA & remedies: we can propose a remedies schedule for outages >=30 mins; options include pro-rated credits or emergency capacity commitments.
- Liability cap: we can consider a 12-month fees cap for liability — Laura from Legal will propose wording.
- Purchase path: Azure Private Plans generally allow marketplace PO flow if the merchant routing is configured; I'll confirm with our marketplace ops and contoso partner.

I'll ask Laura to review Valora's redlines and come back with a counter by EOD Monday. Irene will check marketplace routing with the partner ops team.

If it helps, can the procurement team share any required PO/DocuSign templates?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0199
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@valorahealth.com>, Tom Perez <tom.perez@valorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Valora Health - Azure Private Plan: commercial and procurement questions

Jordan/Irene — I've reviewed Valora's redlines (attached) and drafted a counterproposal addressing their four bullets. Summary of proposed changes (detailed redlines in attached doc):

1) Data residency & logs: add explicit clause: "Customer data, including PHI where applicable, will be processed and stored only within the Azure region designated in Exhibit A; audit logs will be retained for a period of seven (7) years for compliance and audit purposes."

2) SLA & remedies: propose remedies matrix: credits for partial downtime, with an enhanced response SLA and an option for emergency capacity allocation for repeated outages (>=3 incidents of >=30 mins in 90 days triggers an escalation playbook).

3) Liability cap: counter to liability cap equal to the fees paid by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim (excluding passthrough taxes), with carveouts for willful misconduct and data breach.

4) Procurement path: recommend supporting both marketplace PO flow and a direct SOW/PO backup. For marketplace routing we will coordinate with our partner ops (Irene) and Contoso to confirm merchant seller routing and invoice path.

Next steps: Jordan — please review attached counter (Redwood_Countercommercials_20260406.docx). Maya/Tom — if this looks directionally acceptable we can prepare a clean DocuSign to expedite.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Countercommercials_20260406.docx
From: Tom Perez <tom.perez@valorahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@valorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Valora Health - Azure Private Plan: commercial and procurement questions

Team — thanks for the rapid turnaround. We reviewed Redwood's counter internally and Valora's legal has three clarifying asks (see inline comments in your counter):

A) For the 7-year retention: can Redwood confirm that audit logs will be exportable on request (SFTP/secure Share) for regulatory audit purposes?
B) Remedies matrix: prescribe the exact credit calculation method for outages so our finance team can model the impact.
C) Liability carveouts: Valora needs clearer language around third-party claims arising from data processed by subcontractors — specifically, a mutual flowdown obligation.

We're OK with the 12-month fees cap in principle but need the flowdown language prior to committee sign-off. Our procurement group will share a DocuSign routing template and a PO template tonight.

Irene — can you confirm the marketplace merchant routing and whether invoice routing will land in Azure marketplace (preferred) or route through Redwood AR? That will affect our internal routing.

Thanks — will aim to confirm final position by Tue noon.

Regards,

Tom Perez
Senior Procurement Manager
Valora Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@valorahealth.com>, Tom Perez <tom.perez@valorahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Valora Health - Azure Private Plan: commercial and procurement questions (Final steps)

Maya/Tom — great to align. Quick summary of final items and attachments:

• Audit logs export: Redwood confirms we will provide a secure export mechanism (SFTP or Azure Blob with SAS) for audit requests; language added to Exhibit A.
• Remedies calculation: attached is the exact credit calculation table and examples in the SLA exhibit.
• Subcontractor flowdown: Laura added mutual flowdown language requiring Redwood and downstream subcontractors to contractually obligate flowdown of data protection and indemnity terms.
• Marketplace routing: Irene confirmed with Contoso partner — merchant routing to Azure Marketplace is supported for this private plan, and invoice routing can be set to land in Azure marketplace billing (preferred). If Valora prefers direct invoicing, Redwood AR can accept PO routing.

Attached: Signed_SLA_Valora_20260407.pdf (SLA exhibit with credit table) and a clean DocuSign link will follow once you confirm the PO path. Please confirm which invoice path you prefer and whether we should send the DocuSign now.

If you confirm marketplace routing, we'll push the private plan configuration and provide the marketplace purchase instructions to your procurement team by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks — excited to get Valora live.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Signed_SLA_Valora_20260407.pdf
